questions.question: Which features characterise formal writing?
options: Sophisticated vocabulary, no contractions and an objective tone
questions.explanation: Formal writing uses precise vocabulary, avoids contractions, and keeps an objective, professional tone.

questions.question: Which perspective and voice are typical of formal writing?
questions.explanation: Formal writing often uses third person and passive constructions; informal writing uses first/second person and active voice.

questions.question: According to the chapter, is formal or informal register inherently better?
options: Neither — the skill is choosing the right register for audience and purpose
questions.explanation: Context determines appropriateness: neither register is better in itself.

questions.question: Which is the informal counterpart of the formal sentence "The results were obtained through careful analysis"?
options: "We got the results by looking at it carefully."
"The findings were acquired via methodical examination."
questions.explanation: The informal version uses everyday words ("got", "looking at") and active first person instead of passive formal phrasing.

questions.question: When is informal register appropriate?
options: In personal messages, blogs and conversation with friends
questions.explanation: Informal register suits personal and conversational contexts; formal contexts require formal register.
